extracted.intended_audience: Title IX-regulated institutions, rulemaking commenters, policy analysts, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX RIA response and requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble text responding to public comments on the Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) and related rule provisions for Title IX regulations, describing what costs and effects are appropriate to include, baseline/sensitivity assumptions, and specific regulatory obligations (e.g., supportive measures, scope of "education program or activity").

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude costs of underlying incidents from RIA absent causal evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include estimates regarding the cost of incidents of sexual harassment or assault themselves in the calculation of the likely effects of this regulatory action where there is no evidence that Federal Title IX guidance or regulation affects the underlying number of incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department states it has no evidence indicating that Title IX guidance/regulation affects incident rates and therefore declines to include such costs. It notes supportive measures are offered without fee and could reduce complainant costs, but declines to include savings from reduced underlying incidents given uncertainty about take-up and effect size; however, it will include costs of recipients offering supportive measures pursuant to §106.44(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include costs of offering supportive measures (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When supportive measures are required by regulation (see §106.44(a)), RIAs should include the cost to recipients of offering such supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures, as defined in §106.30, are “offered . . . without fee or charge to the complainant or the respondent.” §106.44(a) requires Title IX Coordinators to promptly contact complainants, discuss availability, consider complainant wishes, inform about availability with or without filing a formal complaint, and explain the process for filing. The Department revised cost estimates to include recipients' costs for offering these measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not count transfers of costs as net savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost-shifting between parties or entities (e.g., shifting costs from schools to complainants/respondents) should not be treated as net cost savings in the RIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department agrees transfers are not savings and notes that prior NPRM estimates did not treat transfers as savings. It also recognized it initially failed to include some time burdens on complainants/respondents and revised estimates accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include opportunity cost of complainant/respondent time
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost estimates must include the time burden on complainants and respondents participating in hearings and other processes, using appropriate wage proxies to value that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added burdens for participation. For K–12 students it assumes costs at the Federal minimum wage; for postsecondary students it uses the median hourly wage for all workers ($18.58/hr) as the opportunity cost proxy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use transparent baseline assumptions and public data
rubrics_metrics.description: The RIA must clearly explain the basis for baseline estimates, identify data sources (public where possible), and document assumptions used to derive estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department relied on publicly available data and detailed its assumptions in the NPRM. It acknowledges limits of available high-quality data and requested public input/alternative data to better capture baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sensitivity analysis and alternative estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Where assumptions are uncertain, RIAs must provide sensitivity analysis and alternative estimates to show how results change with different assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department provided alternative estimates in a “Sensitivity Analysis” section to help the public understand the effects of particular assumptions on overall estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include temporally or causally distant effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude effects that are sufficiently temporally and causally distant from implementation (e.g., long-run future tax revenue changes) because they are impractical to quantify reliably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters asked to include lost future tax revenue or reduced future health care costs from fewer incidents; the Department declined, saying those effects are too temporally/causally distant and rely on disputed assumptions that regulations would change access to education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with Executive Order 12866 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must assess all costs and benefits of a proposed rule 'to the fullest extent that these can be usefully estimated' and choose the option that maximizes benefits and minimizes costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commenter alleged an EO 12866 violation; the Department disagreed and stated it made a good-faith effort to account for likely costs and benefits and that the final regulations are economically significant and impose net costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) burden standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Paperwork burden estimates should be accurate, the information collection's quality and usefulness justifiable, and reporting burdens appropriately minimized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters supported the PRA-related burden estimates; the Department noted appreciation of support and maintained PRA compliance considerations in its analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) small-entity analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess potential effects on small entities and describe whether the regulation imposes disproportionate burdens on small entities, and include relevant discussion in the RFA section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reviewed potential effects on small entities, noted burdens may represent a larger proportion of revenues for small entities, but concluded the final regulations do not impose an unreasonable burden on such entities. It added information in the RFA section to clarify magnitude of effects by institution size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure accounting statement clarity (time window and annualization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present cost and savings figures with clear accounting of time windows (e.g., ten-year totals vs. annualized figures) to avoid confusion about where totals come from.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM's $286.4–$367.7 million was a ten-year figure, whereas the Accounting Statement showed annualized (per year) calculations; the Department clarified this distinction in response to commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and, where warranted, revise baseline counts of investigations/formal complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Where baseline numbers (e.g., average investigations per IHE, formal complaints after implementation) are estimated, the RIA should document the basis and revise estimates when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department acknowledged limited data on current investigations and revised its baseline number of investigations at IHEs to 5.70 and estimated formal complaints after implementation to 3.82 based on comments and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for full universe of affected recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: RIAs should identify and include recipients beyond LEAs/IHEs (e.g., museums, libraries, cultural centers) if they receive federal assistance and fall under Title IX coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters highlighted that Title IX reaches private education programs, museums, libraries, etc. The Department analyzed FY2018 grants and added 600 entities to its model, assigning assumptions about their case volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider heterogeneity in recipient responses and potential above-required actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that regulated entities vary in how they respond to rules; include assumptions about what fraction may engage in activities beyond minimal requirements (e.g., retaining attorneys as advisors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department assumed ~45% of postsecondary recipients might adopt measures above requirements and also assumed attorneys would serve as advisors in cost modeling. It revised cost estimates to reflect such heterogeneity where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include costs of advisors/attorneys where likely
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is reasonable to expect recipients or parties will retain attorneys or advisors as part of compliance (e.g., advisors for hearings), include those costs in the RIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued institutions may keep law firms on retainer to serve as advisors; Department noted initial estimates already assumed attorneys would serve as advisors and adjusted where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define scope of 'education program or activity' for coverage of incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory definitions of 'education program or activity' determine whether incidents (including off-campus ones) trigger recipient obligations; this scope affects which incidents are included in obligations and cost estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department clarified the definition includes locations/events over which the recipient exercised substantial control over respondent and context, and buildings owned/controlled by recognized student organizations; recipients must respond to allegations in their program/activity, whether on or off campus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for arbitrary/capricious challenges: cite reasons and limits of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When commenters claim agency conclusions are arbitrary or capricious (e.g., failing to consider perpetrator incentives), RIA/preamble should articulate rationale and limitations of evidence linking regulations to behavioral change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explained why it did not include certain costs and why it does not consider perpetrator behavior to be driven by Title IX guidance/regulation, distinguishing criminal-context evidence from administrative contexts and providing its rationale to counter claims of arbitrary action.
